pk.context: 20 mcg subcutaneous, single dose, healthy adults

pill.desc: clear, colourless solution in a single-patient prefilled pen

tell: A recombinant fragment of parathyroid hormone that builds bone by favoring osteoblast over osteoclast activity.

clues.text: Absolute bioavailability after subcutaneous injection is approximately 95%. Clearance exceeds normal liver plasma flow, which fits both hepatic and extra-hepatic clearance.
Made in Escherichia coli by recombinant DNA technology, with a molecular weight of 4117.8 daltons. It is a free base, not a salt.
Supplied under an NDA as a 560 mcg/2.24 mL solution in a single-patient prefilled pen, delivering 20 mcg per dose for up to 28 days. Dosed once daily.
No boxed warning. Contraindicated after severe hypersensitivity to it or its inactive ingredients; reactions have included anaphylaxis and angioedema.
Postmenopausal osteoporosis at high fracture risk, osteoporosis in men with primary or hypogonadal disease, and glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis.

Binds the same high-affinity receptors as the N-terminal region of parathyroid hormone, with equal affinity. Once-daily dosing favors bone formation through preferential stimulation of osteoblasts over osteoclasts.
The generic name begins with T and has twelve letters.
